Visit Boulder Creek: Redwoods, Town and Local Guide | Boulder Creek Local 0 Come curious, come prepared Visit Boulder Creek A small mountain town at the north end of the San Lorenzo Valley, surrounded by redwoods. Plan ahead, drive for the roads, and leave room for weather and access to change. Confirm hours and conditions with each place before you go. Check conditions Find food and drink Getting here Plan the drive first. Boulder Creek sits on Highway 9. The roads in are winding and mostly two lanes, so give yourself extra time and check conditions before you leave. By car From Santa Cruz, take Highway 9 north up the valley through Felton and Ben Lomond. From the Santa Clara Valley side, Highway 9 climbs over the summit from Saratoga. A common alternative from Highway 17 is Bear Creek Road, which drops into Boulder Creek from the east. All three are slow mountain roads with tight curves, cyclists, and wildlife, so use pullouts to let faster traffic by. Check the roads Winter storms and summer roadwork both close lanes up here. Check Caltrans QuickMap for real-time closures and chain controls, and the County Road Closure Dashboard for local roads. Our Mountain Status page pulls together the same sources. Cell service is patchy along parts of Highway 9, so it helps to have directions saved before you lose signal. Riding the bus? Santa Cruz METRO Routes 35 and 35X connect Boulder Creek and the San Lorenzo Valley with Santa Cruz. The 35X is a weekday express; Route 35 covers nights and weekends. Check the current schedule with METRO before you plan a trip. The redwoods Parks and trails nearby. Access in these parks keeps changing after the 2020 CZU fire. Confirm hours, reservations, and open trails on each official page the day you go. Big Basin Redwoods State Park California's oldest state park is open for limited day-use as it recovers from the CZU fire, and much of it is still closed. Parking is limited and first come, first served. Reservations are encouraged, not required. As of 2026-07-16 the state lists day-use fees of $6 plus a $2 reservation fee, or $10 without a reservation, and no fee to arrive by foot, bike, or bus. There is no drinking water on site except at the kiosk. Confirm the current status before you drive up. Big Basin access, State Parks Castle Rock State Park Sandstone formations and ridge-top views along Skyline. It sits on Highway 35 about two and a half miles southeast of the Highway 9 junction. Parking is $10 a day at a self-serve kiosk, and the gate is locked at sunset. Weekdays are quieter for parking. Castle Rock, State Parks Fall Creek, Henry Cowell A quiet day-use unit with about twenty miles of trails through redwoods and old lime kilns. The trailhead and free parking are on Felton Empire Road off Highway 9. There are no facilities, and dogs, bikes, and fires are not allowed. Henry Cowell, State Parks Closer to town, the Boulder Creek Recreation and Park District keeps up Junction Park , with a small beach, San Lorenzo River access, a lawn, and picnic tables one block off the main street. Barbara Day Park sits just downstream, and Garrahan Park up Highway 9 has a walking track, fields, and barbecue areas. The river is a popular summer swim spot, and it's swim at your own risk. Choose your own adventure A perfect day in Boulder Creek. Five stops, three ways to make each one yours. Hours change up here, so check before you count on any single stop. Start with breakfast Jenna Sue's Coffee and a casual downtown start. The Tree House Cafe The other local coffee stop, made for lingering. Bella's Cafe The town's sit-down breakfast. Earn your lunch Play a round Nine holes under the redwoods at the Boulder Creek Golf and Country Club . Swim The rec district pool in season, or the river beach at Junction Park. Hike Big Basin Limited day-use as the park recovers; check access first . Lunch, three ways Taqueria Los Gallos Burritos and tacos, no ceremony. El Rey Leon Mexican food truck on the main drag. The Sawmill Burgers, pub fare, and outdoor seating. Walk the shops The main stretch rewards a slow lap: Air and Fire for crystals and gifts, SWAG's eclectic collective, Viscosity Glass for locally made glass art, Beck's Shoes, fitting families since 1919, and Scarborough's hardware and garden aisles with a little of everything. The directory has the full list with hours. Stay for dinner Tae's Edo Sushi Bar Sushi and Japanese dinner plates. Scopazzi's Historic Italian dining room and lounge. Red Pearl Chinese, dine-in or takeout. Full details, hours, and phone numbers for every spot are on Food and Drink . Through the year What the seasons ask of you. Conditions shape a visit more than the calendar does. Check before you come. Winter Storms bring downed trees, flooding, and road closures on Highway 9 and the back roads. Check Mountain Status and Caltrans QuickMap before heading up, and turn around if a road looks unsafe. Summer The valley can be warm and the river draws crowds. Bring water, watch your footing on rocks, keep an eye on kids near moving water, and pack out everything you bring. Fire season This is a fire-prone forest. No fires or charcoal outside designated areas, and never during a Red Flag Warning. Check fire weather with the National Weather Service and CAL FIRE before you go. Good to know The practical stuff. There's one gas station in town on Highway 9, so fill up before long drives or a trip out to Big Basin. Groceries and markets are on the food and drink page. Public restrooms are limited, so plan around them. Remember that cell service drops out along stretches of Highway 9. Respect the mountain Visit like a neighbor. Most of what looks like open forest is someone's home, watershed, or working land. Leave no trace and pack out your trash. Don't park on blind curves or block driveways and pullouts. Keep noise down near houses, follow all fire restrictions, and give the road and the river the caution they're due. Keep exploring Build a fuller day. Jobs | Boulder Creek Local 0 Work nearby Jobs in the San Lorenzo Valley The board carries three kinds of work, and it helps to know which is which before you start scrolling. Inside the valley, openings are scarce, and most of them come from San Lorenzo Valley Unified. The district is the largest employer up here by a wide margin, and its instructional assistant, coaching and substitute positions turn over through the year. Within commuting distance there's a good deal more: the county's other school districts, the County Office of Education, Cabrillo College, city and county agencies, and retail and hospitality in Santa Cruz, Scotts Valley, Aptos and Capitola. These show an estimated drive time on each card, and anything genuinely far, like Watsonville, is marked as an extended commute and kept off the local tab unless you ask for it. Remote roles open to people in California sit on their own tab. The board refreshes each morning, and the date it last ran is at the top, so you can see how current it is. Before you take the on-site job Santa Cruz is about 30 minutes from Boulder Creek on a clear day and considerably longer when Highway 9 is wet, dark, or closed. San Jose is roughly the same 30 minutes over Bear Creek Road, in good conditions and can be twice that at commute times. Winter storms close Highway 9 more often than newcomers expect, and a closure turns a short drive into a long detour through Felton or over the summit. None of that makes a commute a bad idea. Plenty of people here do it happily. It's worth driving the route at the hour you'd actually be driving it before you commit to it. What this board doesn't have A lot of valley work never gets posted anywhere. Trades, caregiving, cleaning, landscaping, seasonal help and shop shifts are usually filled by word of mouth or a sign in a window. For that kind of work the directory is a better starting point than any job board: find the businesses you'd want to work for, and ask them directly. Listings link back to wherever the job was posted. For school and remote roles that's usually a job board, EDJOIN for the districts and We Work Remotely or Remotive for remote work. City and county agencies, and larger employers, more often link to their own application system. Boulder Creek Local isn't the employer and doesn't handle applications, so confirm the details at the source before you apply. The valley has very little rental stock, a good share of it changes hands privately, and what does get listed tends to go quickly. A short list here isn't a sign the board is broken. It's an accurate picture of a thin market. Listings cover long-term rentals in Boulder Creek, Ben Lomond, Brookdale and Felton, drawn from property managers and public listings. Each one shows when it was last confirmed, so you can tell a fresh listing from a stale one, and each links back to its original source. The board refreshes each morning, and the date it last ran is shown at the top. Before you send anyone money Never wire money, send a deposit, or pay an application fee before you've seen the place in person and confirmed who you're dealing with. Rental scams follow tight markets, and this is one. A listing that pressures you to pay quickly, or asks you to pay before viewing, is a listing to walk away from. Boulder Creek Local isn't the landlord, the property manager, or a party to any agreement. We publish what's listed publicly, and we can be wrong. The rest of the market Because so much of the valley's renting happens outside listing sites, people who find places here usually do it by being visible locally: the community boards on Facebook, a note at the market, telling neighbors you're looking. Most valley rentals are filled before they're ever advertised, and that matches what turns up on this board. If you're new to the area, Resident Resources covers what to sort out once you land: water, power, trash, internet, and what living on a septic system and a mountain road actually involves.
